content:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to decide the runtime shape for locality-weighting. currently it's spread across router+policy, which makes testing and rollout painful.
devon: I found two pain points: 1) regional preference is baked as a transformer in the router, 2) cost/latency heuristics live in the policy DSL. makes small changes require full deploys.
ron: +1. Also the telemetry hooks are inconsistent — sometimes the router emits probe signals, sometimes the policy does. hard to correlate.
maya: Proposal: extract a small LocalityScorer interface that is pure-functional and side-effect free. Runtime will call scorer(request, signals) -> list of (route, score). scorer impls can be swapped via feature flag.
priya: Sounds good. A couple of questions: how do we handle tenant overrides? tenant wants to pin to region or prefer dedicated GPUs. Do we fold that into the scorer input or into a post-filter?
devon: My vote: include tenant-level constraints as part of the input. Scorer returns scores for routes that are compatible with constraints; router can still apply admission controls after scoring. keeps scoring deterministic.
ron: We should also define a clear compatibility check API: is_compatible(route, constraints) -> bool. Then scorer can be implemented without knowing internals of route metadata.
maya: Agreed. Minimal interface: score(request_features, telemetry_snapshot, constraints) -> [(route_id, float)] and is_compatible(route_meta, constraints) -> bool. Keep it language-agnostic (we might run wasm later).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary tests for scorer v2 scheduled for tonight (window: 02:00-03:00 UTC) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
priya: For rollout: feature flag keyed by tenant id so we can land on small tenants first. Also need a migration path for existing policy DSL rules that reference region_penalty and cost_cap.
devon: Migration approach idea: compile DSL region_penalty(...) -> scorer-compatible weight adjustments. Add a translator step in the policy compiler that emits a scorer config JSON. Example config: ```json
{"version":"scorer.v1","weights":{"latency_ms":0.6,"cost_usd":0.3,"region_pref":0.1}}
```
maya: Nice. That lets us keep backward compatibility without duplicate logic. Also we can A/B different score functions for the same tenant (scorerA vs scorerB) for evals.
ron: Telemetry: scorer should return explainability hints (reason codes + contributing signals) so the Console can show why a route was chosen. e.g., `[{route: r1, score:0.42, hints:["low_cost","probe_fresh"]}]`. Keep hints small strings.
priya: Ops concern: scoring must be cheap (<200us) on the fast path. If we move too much into scorer we risk latency SLOs. Are we OK with more approximate scoring?
devon: We can do progressive scoring: cheap fast pass (cost+latency proxies) then a hedging pass for borderline requests. Configurable via per-tenant thresholds.
maya: Implementation plan: 1) spec LocalityScorer interface + compatibility API, 2) add scorer-config translator in policy-compiler, 3) implement scorer in router as a pluggable module w/ wasm shim, 4) add telemetry/explainability contract, 5) canary rollout behind tenant feature-flag.
priya: Please add a short checklist for SRE: fallbacks if scorer crashes, and metric names (scorer.latency, scorer.cache_hit, scorer.degraded_fallback).
maya: Will add checklist as PR comment. Also we should add an integration test that runs DSL -> scorer-config -> scorer and validates identical output for a few seeded cases.
ron: One more: define how scoring interacts with prewarming/leases. If scorer prefers region that has no warm pools, router must be allowed to preemptively provision or apply a penalty. Add a `warmth` field to telemetry_snapshot.
devon: Exactly. telemetry_snapshot = {latency_p95, cost_est, warm_pool_size, probe_age_ms}. Keep fields small.
maya: OK I'll open an RFC follow-up with the interface and migration steps. tagging @devon @priya for review. Thanks all :thumbsup:
